correspondence.component_scope: eastern opening and southward valley
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern opening lies in a pale dry valley among dissected hills. Its southeastward descent and southward turn remain within the same valley/fan approach, distinguished from the larger neighboring ravines. No headwater hydronym is supplied by the photograph.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southwestern fan receiving plain
correspondence.finding: The opening broadens into a diffuse alluvial approach and turns southwest across the receiving plain below the hill fronts. Pale branching traces and the uninterrupted low depositional floor account for the joins and westward continuation. Roads cross this floor but are not mistaken for channel evidence. A presently wet thread or exact bank alignment is not needed for this ordinary fan-to-plain correspondence.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southern plain bend and westward receiver
correspondence.finding: The selected route swings south around the end of the southern upland and joins a broad, pale westward depositional corridor. This turns northwest along the foot of the low western hills. The overview and overlapping western detail show one receiving floor rather than an intervening mountain divide. No name or present discharge is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestern alluvial playa approach
correspondence.finding: The receiving corridor continues northwest through a broad mixture of alluvium and pale playa-margin deposits. It follows the foot of dissected hills, joins the central saline/depression floor, and skirts small local higher patches. The closely inspected original detail supports the ordinary floor connection; the selected line is not interpreted as a surveyed channel through every salt patch.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: central playa margin and westward low passage
correspondence.finding: The selected sequence turns northwest and west through the low depositional passage along the margins of adjacent pale playa basins, then bends south around a low hill nose. The closer image shows a continuous low receiving-floor setting around the higher ground. It does not establish present spill direction, lake-level thresholds or a continuously wetted inter-lake channel.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: western receiving depression and actual end
correspondence.finding: The final sequence follows the pale western depression margin, bends west through the receiving basin floor and ends on an inner depositional/locally vegetated tongue beside pale and bluish pan surfaces. The stored source and render endpoints coincide, but each is retained as its own endpoint description. This is the actual selected interior-basin ending, not a substituted outer shoreline, surveyed river mouth or continuation to another lake.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: dry alluvial and saline basin environment
correspondence.finding: All selected parts have been accounted for as eastern dry valley/fan approaches, an open alluvial plain, low connected playa-margin passages and the western receiving depression. Local salt pans and dry patches do not in themselves constitute missing geographic links. No glacier, large managed waterbody or supported engineered interbasin transfer is involved in the inspected corridor. Neither one continuously flowing natural river nor its whole-feature name is established.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

endpoint_descriptions.source_endpoint: The pinned source endpoint is in the inner western receiving depression, on a depositional/locally vegetated tongue rather than a surveyed outer-shore mouth.
endpoint_descriptions.render_endpoint: The render endpoint coincides with the source endpoint in the pinned record; its photographed setting is the same inner depression tongue.
endpoint_descriptions.limits: Neither present standing-water extent nor current inflow/spill direction is established. The lake name is not independently pinned to this exact pan.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen eastern opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening and initial westward bend lie in the contiguous mapped Inland Ice, southeast of southern Hall Land. Blue inland-ice contours and ice-thickness shading are not river channels.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: westward inland ice passage
correspondence.finding: The selection continues west across the same uninterrupted mapped ice terrain, bending slightly south before its westward middle reach. The national original covers this entire interval; no missing basin transfer is inferred from the absence of a mapped river.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: turn to petermann side margin
correspondence.finding: The route turns north through the continuous ice margin beside exposed-bedrock spurs on the east side of the named Petermann Gletscher corridor. The original distinguishes bedrock, ice and nearby glacier trough; no exact modern river banks or hydraulic route is claimed.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northern margin and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The selected northward continuation, westward step and final northern bend end in the historical ice-margin setting immediately south of Hall Land and east of the main Petermann glacial trough. Source and render endpoints occupy this same ordinary geographic setting, with the render extension slightly farther northwest. The selected endpoint is not extended to Hall Bassin and is not asserted to be an ordinary river mouth or the present glacier front.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

terminal_details.source_endpoint_description: Historical ice-margin setting south of Hall Land and immediately east of the Petermann glacial trough.
terminal_details.render_endpoint_description: Slightly farther northwest than the stored source ending, in the same regional historical ice-margin setting.
terminal_details.limits: Stored sea class is preserved, not revalidated. No exact contemporary land/ice/water assignment, glacier front, ordinary river mouth or subglacial discharge is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Chiricahua Mountains canyon and its western emergence
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening occupies the mapped Turkey Creek canyon on the western side of the Chiricahua Mountains. The inspected upper view follows the canyon westward past its side-canyon junctions into the open piedmont. This is the selected start, not a claim to identify the officially defined headwater or source point.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward fan passage and Rock Creek receiving junction
correspondence.finding: Turkey Creek continues across the mountain-front fan, bends northwest and receives the mapped Rock Creek corridor from the north. The selected continuation is the Turkey Creek receiving branch. Rock Creek is contextual joining drainage, not a separate selected FID or an alias for Turkey Creek. The Ash, Stanford and Pridham corridors to the south are distinguishable neighboring drainage.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Open agricultural and alluvial floor between upper fan and lower Turkey Creek reach
correspondence.finding: The selected westward passage traverses the continuous low-relief valley floor toward the lower mapped Turkey Creek reach beside Sulphur Hills. Map linework is discontinuous across parts of this agricultural plain, but the ordinary-scale receiving floor and westward slope corridor are continuous. No intervening ridge, separate enclosed basin or required lake-to-feeder transfer is indicated. Correspondence uses that floor rather than inventing a named blue-line channel or a current operating route through field drains.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower labeled reach west of Sulphur Hills and northward approach to the playa
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the lower Turkey Creek setting west of Sulphur Hills, then continues north across the common gently sloping receiving plain into the playa margin. The map depicts the lower creek and its northward dissipation within this continuous floor. The subsequent plain passage is geographically established at ordinary corridor scale without extending the creek name over each modeled connector or assuming a continuously wet thread.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Playa entry, interior continuation and actual modeled ending
correspondence.finding: The remaining selected parts turn through the large lakebed south of Willcox and end within its interior. National Map cartography establishes the common receiving lakebed, while AZGFD authorial prose identifies Willcox Playa as an alkaline lakebed that floods seasonally. The selected ending is within that playa, not a stream mouth on an open coast, an external-basin outlet or a claim to select the entire lakebed. Nearby Cochise Lakes and Crane Lake are not substituted for this ending.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

terminal_distinctions.source_endpoint_description: Stored source ending is in the Willcox Playa interior, after the selected route has passed through the common northern receiving floor and lakebed.
terminal_distinctions.render_endpoint_description: Stored render ending occupies the same playa-interior receiving setting; it does not establish a new outlet or a named river mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen northeastern opening and westward upper route
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and long southwestward upper route require original terrain coverage. Regional historical glacier descriptions do not locate every chosen part or establish its named glacier and receiving valley. No upper glacier name is assigned.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle feeder to lower regional drainage
correspondence.finding: The selected southern feeder and southwestward bend lie within the geographic study area of the independent regional source, but its prose is not exact selected-path correspondence. Regional Bering River and nearby lake descriptions are retained only as bounded context; no selected lake traversal or named confluence is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering within the sole selected mainstem fragment.

correspondence.finding: The final selected southward approach and actual source/render ending require direct geographic evidence. Neither the named Bering River mouth nor the full historical Bering Lake drainage can be substituted for this selected eastern ending. Both stored ending positions are preserved, with the render endpoint farther south and slightly west than the source endpoint.
